parsed.explanation: The dossier's worst feature is a live, trans-specific appearance offence (Section 379) that turns on dress alone, reaches a trans woman visitor in any public space, carries up to three months' imprisonment, and has no remedy: no hate-crime or anti-discrimination law, no functioning LGBTI civil society (the one group raided and shuttered in 2017), and most openly LGBTI citizens have fled. Surrounding that statute are documented security-force harassment, arrest, detention, torture and beatings of LGBTI persons across 2018–2022, and a 2017 ministerial call to arrest and detain them. That is state-directed coercion with severe custody risk, not mere social disapproval. Offsetting it: the dossier sources no actual enforcement or prosecution under Section 379 or the unenforced conduct provision, and the ministerial order was not shown to be carried out. Unenforced paper plus documented custodial violence and zero recourse puts this well below the 0.35 tiers, short of the 0.15 enforcement tier.
